newsitem.title: GERMANY: German aluminium smelters aim for full capacity.
newsitem.headline: German aluminium smelters aim for full capacity.

text.p: Sources at German primary aluminium smelters said they were aiming to run their plants at full capacity in 1997 in response to strong demand.
VAW aluminium AG had no plans to change output schedules from the 317,000 tonnes produced at its German operations in 1996, spokesman Volker Karow said.
"Production in 1997 should continue to run at 1996 levels, which nearly matched our full capacity," he said.
VAW in 1995 produced 377,000 tonnes in Germany. It also has overseas shareholdings in Canadian and Australian smelters.
This year, it phased out its smelter at Toeging and raised output at three others in Germany.
Board member Karl Wobbe said on Tuesday orders were looking up well into 1997.
VAW is part of utility group VIAG AF.
At Aluminium Essen GmbH, 1996 targets for primary output were being met, a company official confirmed.
Some 94,800 tonnes were produced in 1996, little changed from 1995.
The Essen smelter planned to produce 95,000-96,000 tonnes in 1997, he said.

He also put casthouse production a 122,000 tonnes in 1996 after 130,000 tonnes in 1995 as slabs and billets customers slowed down their purchases this year when their own orders dropped, especially in the second quarter.
Essen planned to produce 130,000-140,000 tonnes of slabs and billets next year if orders held up well, he added.

At Hamburger Aluminium-Werk GmbH (HAW), some 119,500 tonnes of primary aluminium would be produced in 1996, according to managing director Dieter Leibetseder, who a year ago gave a 121,000 tonne target for 1996 and a 119,000 figure for 1995.
He said the company's 1997 output should be 120,000 tonnes.
The plant is owned by VAW, Austria Metall AG, and Reynolds Aluminium Deutschland Inc., a unit of U.S. Reynolds Metals Co..
Its output, which comes under the three owners' totals, is fully absorbed by their downstream operations through a network of contracts.
